cells.tense: The read and the saying land together now, and the road ahead is being spoken as it is walked.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Say the direction out loud to someone on this road — not the case for it, just where it points — and take their questions as they come, sometime before the week is out.
cells.core:
You read the road while you move on it, and the reading reaches your voice quickly. People on this road know where you stand without having to dig for it, and that is uncommon: clarity and speech arriving in the same breath, nothing held back for later.

What the balance is free to feed next is where that reading gets handed on. Name the direction to one person — not the argument, the direction — and take their questions as they come. You'll hear which parts only hold inside your own head. A read kept private stays a private read. A read spoken becomes something the two of you share, and shared reads are what turn a road into a place people can walk together.

cells.tense: The judgement has run ahead of the moment, and the answer is fixed before the road has shown you anything.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Before the next push, give the drive one small feed — a call, a line, a thing that genuinely lights you — and stop when the warmth shows. Let that warmth size the next stage.
cells.core:
The reading of the road is happening before the road has shown itself. Verdicts are ready, positions are set, and the case for the direction is already written, weighing more than the walking does. The people with you can feel the difference even where the reasoning is sound, because nothing is surprising you anymore.

What this needs is the opposite of a bigger plan. Before the next push, give the drive one small feed — a call, a line, a thing that genuinely lights you — and stop when the warmth shows. Then let that warmth set the size of the next stage. A drive fed a little at a time stays warm enough to be moved by something other than the answer you already have.

cells.tense: The judgement is still sharp, and it has been standing at a door the push already walked through.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Ask one person on this road how it's going for them, and stay in their answer until you've heard it whole — no solving it, no steering it, just the listening.
cells.core:
The judgement is still there and still sharp. What has stopped is the moving. The direction gets read from behind, watching, and no weight goes into the push. The read is accurate and it isn't being spent on anything, which is how a clear head ends up at a door the rest of the person has already gone through.

Pushing into the starved place won't bring it back. Someone else's feeling will. Ask one person on this road how it's going for them, then stay in their answer until you've heard it whole. The pull comes back through the connection, not through the push, and asking is doing something real in a seat that is stuck.

cells.tense: The steadying of the direction is being done and called getting on, with no one's name on the doing.
cells.act: pursue the emotional truth with someone
cells.ask: Ask one person on this road the question you actually want answered — the real one, not the safe one — and keep the conversation going past the first answer.
cells.core:
You keep the direction level under pressure, and your own account calls it getting on with the work. Ask the people on this road and they will name what you are holding steady. The work is real and constant; your telling of it leaves your hand out of the frame.

This began smaller, with one other person, before it scaled into holding the line for a whole road. Ask one person on this road the question you actually want answered — the real one, not the safe one — and keep the conversation going past the first answer. The first form of this was relational, not managerial. Begin there and the credit comes back where it belongs.

The sentence that serves me more than them is the Too Little seedling line about tending the push like something young, which is pretty but asks for no visible motion in a seat that is made of motion.
